subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fastretailco.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@fastretailco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before the load test. Good to hear the primary goals: validating our latency SLOs under realistic traffic and confirming streaming behavior with chunked responses.

Recap / targets discussed
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 750ms (end-to-end server-side generation)
- Error rate: < 0.5% for 5xx responses
- Throughput: target sustained 1200 requests/min (20 rps) with peaks up to 50 rps
- Concurrency: up to 250 concurrent sessions (simulating 250 active users)
- Streaming: responses must start streaming within 100-200ms of first token and maintain chunking behavior for clients that use Transfer-Encoding: chunked

Load test coordination items (next steps for customer-led run)
1) Customer to run k6/Locust test against our test endpoint — we attached a starter k6 script (k6-load-test-script-v1.js) for your team to iterate on.
2) Please confirm a 2-hour test window (we suggested Tue 2026-03-17 09:00-11:00 PT). If that doesn't work, propose alternatives.
3) We'll provide a scoped test API key and test account; Dev (cc'd) will send credentials and IP ranges to whitelist.
4) Please send the exact scripts/traffic profile you plan to run (vus, arrival rate, payload sizes) and where streaming behavior is exercised.
5) We'll monitor the run via our staging Grafana and share p95/p99, error rates, GPU utilization, and token throughput in real time.

Attachments: k6-load-test-script-v1.js (application/javascript, stub)

Open questions for you: do you need sustained tokens/sec metrics instead of requests/sec? Also confirm whether clients will use long-lived connections (SSE/WebSocket) or short polling.

Thanks — I can coordinate a brief pre-test check 30 minutes before the window.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fastretailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@fastretailco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few quick items from our side:

1) Window: Tue the 17th conflicts with a customer release. Can we shift to Wed 2026-03-18 08:00-10:00 PT? That works for our platform team.
2) Scripts: attaching our internal k6 script and a short Locust scenario (we'll link the repo). We'll be simulating both short prompts (avg 60 tokens) and longer generation flows (avg 800 tokens) to exercise KV cache and attention ramps.
3) Streaming: we'll validate streaming by opening a streaming client and measuring time-to-first-byte and chunk intervals.
4) IPs: please provide the CIDR blocks you want us to whitelist on our side; we'll also need the IPs your test runners will come from — can you provide yours?

Attaching: fastretail-k6-scenario.js (we uploaded to our gist)

On the SLOs: p95 300ms lines up with our expectations, but we need to see p99 for tail behavior — we'll measure both.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Alex — thanks. Providing the test artifacts from our side below.

What we're provisioning for the run:
- Scoped test API key: READ/INFER only; rate-limited and expires after the test window.
- Test endpoint: https://staging-infer.redwood.ai/v1/fastretail-test
- IPs to whitelist (outbound from our runners): 34.200.0.0/16, 18.234.0.0/16
- Please whitelist: 52.24.0.0/16 for our telemetry hooks (Grafana push).

Attachment: test-account-credentials.txt (contains test_api_key=REDACTED and sample curl)
Attachment: ip-allowlist-request.pdf (list + justification)

Notes on traffic shaping:
- If you run token-heavy flows (800 tokens), we'll recommend a lower VU count but higher arrival-rate to preserve concurrency characteristics.
- We will enable streaming compatibility on the test endpoint — ensure client tests open connections for at least 3s for stream measurement.

If you confirm Wed 2026-03-18 08:00-10:00 PT, we'll provision the key and post a pre-test readiness check 30m before start.

—Dev

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Quick note on observability and what we'll monitor during the window:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 (server-side generation)
- Error rate: 4xx vs 5xx breakdown and request retry behavior
- Token throughput: tokens/sec and tokens/min (important for cost/throughput tradeoffs)
- GPU metrics: utilization, memory pressure, soft-fail signals from the runtime
- Concurrency: active sessions, open connections, and queue depth

I'll prepare a short checklist for the pre-test readiness check:
- Verify test API key works with a simple curl (streaming vs non-streaming)
- Confirm client can open a streaming connection and receive incremental chunks
- Validate sampling on our tracing (we'll enable 10% sample for the run)
- Baseline GPU utilization for the first 15 minutes

Link: https://redwood-inference.app/docs/load-testing (runbook)

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fastretailco.com>

Date: 2026-03-16T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

All right — Wed 2026-03-18 08:00-10:00 PT is confirmed from our side. We've shared our k6/Locust scenarios with the platform team and will run two passes:
- Pass A: short prompts (60 tokens avg), ramp to 20 rps sustain for 60 minutes
- Pass B: long generation (800 tokens avg), burst to 50 rps for 10 min, then back to 15 rps

We will exercise streaming by opening a streaming client in Pass B.
Checklist requests from our side:
- Please confirm the exact test API key name you'll provide and the expiration time.
- Confirm the CIDR blocks you listed in this thread are the full set we'll see traffic from.
- What's the expected behavior if we exceed rate limits? Will we see 429s or queued requests?
We'll post our final scripts in the gist by EOD tomorrow. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fastretailco.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-16T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Thanks Alex — confirmed. Quick answers:
- Test API key name: fastretail-test-20260318 (expires 2026-03-18T12:15:00-07:00)
- CIDR blocks we'll use: 34.200.0.0/16, 18.234.0.0/16 (Dev also included 52.24.0.0/16 for telemetry).
- Rate limiting behavior: you'll receive 429s when a per-key rate limit is hit; we will not silently queue requests on the gateway. We recommend backing off and retrying with jitter for client behavior validation.

Pre-test cadence:
- Wed 07:30 PT: pre-test readiness check (15m) — verify key, streaming, and basic metrics
- Wed 08:00 PT: start Pass A
- Wed 09:10 PT: start Pass B
- Wed 09:50 PT: cool-down and initial analysis
We'll join the platform team Slack channel during the run and share Grafana links. If anything looks off we'll abort and diagnose — agreed approach is to stop and pivot rather than continue to a failing run.
Looking forward — we'll be on standby.
—Marissa
